name: Corners Factor through Cartesian Products
statement: For nonempty Boolean classes $A$ and $B$ on disjoint coordinate sets, the maximal cubes of $A\times B$ are exactly the products of maximal cubes of the factors. A vertex $(a,b)$ is a corner exactly when both $a$ and $b$ are corners. Hence a cornerless product has a cornerless factor; for ample factors that factor is again ample.
proof: Every cube in the product factors uniquely over the two coordinate blocks, and it is maximal exactly when both factor cubes are maximal. The number of maximal cubes through $(a,b)$ is therefore the product of the corresponding two counts, which equals one exactly when both counts equal one. Ampleness also factors through Cartesian products.
